details.description: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B is the 1.5-billion-parameter base checkpoint in Alibaba's Qwen2.5-Coder family, first open-sourced by the Qwen team on September 19, 2024, alongside the 7B size. It was pretrained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, text-code grounding data, and synthetic data. As a base (non-instruct) model, Qwen states it is not meant for direct conversational use and instead serves as a foundation for fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or continued pretraining.
advantages: Pretrained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, text-code grounding data, and synthetic data, per Qwen's model card.
Supports a full 32,768-token context window despite its compact 1.5B parameter size, per Qwen's model card.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license, permitting commercial use and redistribution.
disadvantages: Is a base model, not tuned for instructions; Qwen states it does not recommend using base language models for conversations and instead recommends fine-tuning, RLHF, or continued pretraining.
Text-only input and output, with no vision or audio support.
At 1.5B parameters, it is one of the smaller checkpoints in the six-size Qwen2.5-Coder family (0.5B to 32B), trading model capacity for lower resource use.
use_cases: Fine-tuning into lightweight, latency-sensitive coding assistants or on-device coding tools.
Continued pretraining or RLHF starting point for building smaller custom code models.
Code completion and generation research or benchmarking on resource-constrained hardware.

notes: Base (non-instruct) checkpoint. Corrected the open-source date: the Nov 12, 2024 family post explicitly says 1.5B/7B were already open-sourced before that post; the original Qwen2.5-Coder launch post dates the 1.5B/7B release to September 19, 2024. Also added base-model benchmark scores (HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, BigCodeBench-Complete) from the Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report (arXiv 2409.12186), which reports per-size scores for base checkpoints that the family blog post omits.
